service.description: A change marker on the time series (source deploy, config, release or user: MONITOR_INGEST or the monitor_annotations dataset's create), or a business event (source business; docs/tools/Monitoring.md "Business events"): a domain's event with its name, time, organization, type (event) and the record behind it (recordType, recordId) or a link on this server, and no amount. A business event needs the artifact org.moqui.report.annotation.business (create), which its owning service passes by writing with authorization off after its commit; MONITOR_INGEST does not write one. With an eventKey the event keeps one marker, written again in place.

From a value of a saved panel to its breakdown and records (crates/moqui-report/src/drill.rs; docs/tools/Monitoring.md "Drill"). The request names a definition the viewer reads (a dashboard with panelId, or a library panel), one of the panel's queries (queryReference, its index) and the buckets chosen (selectedBuckets: field, value as the panel showed them); never a query, entity or service. The engine runs the panel as its dashboard does (variables fill the saved variables only; each dataset's admission and row filter apply), takes each bucket's predicate from its own result (an Other or missing bucket keeps its exact predicate), and answers the saved query narrowed by them: selected, the panel's own frames (panelFrames), dimensions, an optional breakdown by one of the dataset's dimensions, and a page of records with columns, total and bounded. A viewer who reads the dataset's aggregates and not its records (rows restricted) gets rowsAvailable false with rowsReason and no record; a panel the viewer cannot read answers available false with its reason.

Delete a saved definition the viewer owns, with its versions and an alert rule's state. Shipped and read-only definitions cannot be deleted, nor one that other definitions still reference. Git syncs remove its file.
Records an export of report data done outside the report services, such as the Explore document download.

The business datasets (signal business) the viewer may read, each with its source, scope policy, admission checks and state (admitted, review, retired, unavailable); a steward (org.moqui.report.dataset update) also sees those of theirs waiting for review.

The admission checks of one business dataset for its steward: its document in a registered DataFeed, its index built (and not older than its last field change), its rowFilterService a registered scope policy.

A steward's business dataset over a DataDocument a registered DataFeed indexes, with a registered scope policy and its parameters, saved as a dataset definition they own and waiting for review. Refuses a document of no feed, a telemetry index, an unregistered policy, a group the steward is not in, and an id whose own update artifact (org.moqui.report.dataset.(id)) the creator does not hold: a prefix a screen puts before a name gives no right.

Rebuild one business dataset's index: org.moqui.search.SearchServices.index#DataFeedDocuments for its feed and its document only, for its steward (the dataset's update artifact), recording when and how many.

A steward adds, revises and removes a business dataset's document fields (fields: fieldSeqId, fieldPath, fieldNameAlias, functionName, sequenceNum, remove). A new path is plain (no expression or secret field); names stay unique; removing or renaming a field a definition over the dataset names is refused until it is revised, as is a stale expectedVersion. The index is stale until rebuilt.

A steward adds, revises and removes the conditions that narrow a business dataset's document (conditions: conditionSeqId, fieldNameAlias, operator, fieldValue, toFieldNameAlias, remove), each on a field of the document with an operator of the list; never a post-query expression, and never in place of the row filter.

One business dataset the caller reads or stewards (dataset: as find#BusinessDatasets answers it, with readable, stewarded and the scope policy's scopeParameter), and for its steward the fields of its document (fields: fieldSeqId, fieldPath, fieldNameAlias, fieldName, functionName, sequenceNum, expression), the conditions that narrow it (conditions: conditionSeqId, fieldNameAlias, operator, fieldValue, toFieldNameAlias, postQuery) and the definitions over it that the caller reads (uses: id, title, type, readOnly; usesAvailable false when they could not be listed). A reader who does not steward it gets the dataset alone. A dataset the caller neither reads nor stewards is refused as one that is not available, as one that does not exist is.

What a business dataset's forms may offer, for a signed-in caller: the registered scope policies (policies: scopePolicyId, description, scopeParameter, the name of the rowFilterParameters entry in which a dataset names the field that carries a row's scope, from the policy's registration, null where it registers none), the condition operators and field functions a steward may use (operators, functions), whether the caller may create a dataset (canCreate: the dataset-save artifact org.moqui.report.dataset, update, by the caller's own grant) and, only then, the documents a dataset may be made over (documents: dataDocumentId, documentName, indexName; those of registered data feeds, never a telemetry index). It takes nothing from the request.

The framework's scope policy ReportUserGroups (ReportSetupData.xml), a business dataset's rowFilterService: the rows whose field named in rowFilterParameters (groupField, userGroupId by default) is one of the signed-in viewer's user groups; nothing for a viewer of none. A userId of another user is refused. A domain registers its own policies (an organization's, a confidential class's) the same way, each with its scope parameter (here groupField) as the enumeration's optionValue.

return.message: The user group row filter is computed for the signed-in user only
Group field ${groupField} is not a field name

service.description: The report schedules the viewer owns (one of them with screenScheduledId), each with its definition, timing, delivery mode (empty for an owner-mode schedule, personal or group), recipients, revision, pause reason and last run.
Pause or resume a schedule the viewer owns. Resuming a group schedule repeats the audience check (check#ReportAudience) and is refused while a recipient's scope differs from the owner's.

Whether each proposed recipient of a report or dashboard the viewer would own a schedule of, or of an alert rule the viewer reads, may be sent the viewer's own result: an internal, active user with an address whose scope fingerprint for the definition equals the viewer's. The fingerprint is a hash of what the user reads of the definition and everything it references, the documents of each dataset they may read and each dataset's resolved row filter (rowFilter, contextFilters and the rowFilterService's answer). Groups are expanded to their members in date and each is checked. recipients names each one (userId, username, userFullName, viaGroupIds, eligible, blocking, reasonCode, reason); a reason is a code (not-shared: the definition or one it references is not theirs to read; scope-differs; not-comparable for a service source; denied-source; inactive; external; no-address) and never another user's grants. recipientCap is the cap asked for, 50 by default, held under the instance preference report.groupRecipientCeiling; overCap says the audience is larger. Recipients other than the viewer need the artifact org.moqui.report.delivery.group.

Create or change a business report schedule the viewer owns, delivered by email only. The server sets the delivery mode: personal when the owner is the only recipient, group otherwise. A group schedule is saved only when check#ReportAudience passes every recipient (a refused one is an error naming each with its reason code, RECIPIENT_REFUSED) and the audience is within the cap (RECIPIENT_CAP); a change needs the revision read (expectedRevision, STALE_REVISION), and cancels the deliveries of the earlier revision not yet sent. A value not sent is kept: recipient lists not sent keep the recipients (an empty list names the owner alone), and clearFields names which of emailSubject, fromDate and thruDate to empty. At each run the check repeats and a recipient whose scope changed is skipped (scope-differs).

The occurrences of business report schedules, newest first, as status and safe counters, never content: those of the viewer's own schedules (one schedule's with screenScheduledId); with received true, those that hold a delivery to the viewer, each with that delivery's state alone; with administrative true, every owner's, for a holder of ADMIN_TRANSFER_VIEW, without titles.

One occurrence: for its schedule's owner, or a holder of ADMIN_TRANSFER_VIEW, what ran (schedule and revision, definition and version, counters, and its owner by id and by name, ownerUserId and ownerName) and each recipient's outcome (identity, state, safe reason, attempt time, whether it may be retried); for a recipient who is neither, their own delivery only. No frame, file or query diagnostic of anyone's.

The report of one delivery, for its own recipient only. Nothing sent is stored: the report is rendered again as the recipient, with their current authorization, and says so (rerendered, generatedDate). A recipient whose scope fingerprint is no longer the one the delivery was sent under gets available false with reasonCode scope-changed and no content; another user's delivery id is refused as one that does not exist.

Send again to the failed recipients of an occurrence, for its schedule's owner: only deliveries in the failed state (a sent one is never replayed, an uncertain one is refused until reconcile#ReportRecipient settles it), at the occurrence's revision read (expectedRevision), with the same schedule revision and definition version (else DEFINITION_CHANGED: send a new occurrence). Each recipient is checked again as at a run; the report is rendered again and the delivery says so. results names each delivery's outcome.
Settle an uncertain delivery, for its schedule's owner: outcome sent (the message did arrive) or failed (it did not, so it may be retried), with the reason kept in the audit log.

Who may be proposed and accepted as a recipient of a report schedule or an alert rule, for a caller who may deliver to others (canDeliver: the artifact org.moqui.report.delivery.group, create, by the caller's own grant, as check#ReportAudience and store#Schedule ask it): a page of the active internal accounts (users: userId, username, name; found by term in the full name or the username, ignoring case; pageSize, 20 by default, at most 100), the caller's own groups (groups: userGroupId, description; never ALL_USERS: a delivery goes to a group its owner belongs to), and of the users and groups named (userIds, groupIds) which may be recipients (selectedUsers, with their names) and which may not (refusedUserIds, refusedGroupIds). With permissionId only the holders of that permission (members in date of a group that holds it in date) are proposed and accepted: an app that keeps its reports to its own readers passes theirs. The caller is always accepted. A caller who may not deliver to others is answered no account and no group, and every other user and every group named is refused. Being accepted grants nothing: the engine checks each recipient's scope when the schedule or the rule is saved and again before each message.

The screen schedules the caller set up for themselves (a ScreenScheduled of a screen path with the caller as its user and no report definition, as a saved find's scheduled delivery; a report schedule is list#Schedules'), one of them with screenScheduledId (schedules: screenScheduledId, screenPath, formListFindId, description, the saved find's; cronExpression, renderMode, noResultsAbort, paused, fromDate, thruDate, emailSubject, userGroupId, and groupAdmitted: whether the group it names is sent to, which needs its screen path registered as a ReportLegacyAdapter). Another user's schedule is not answered, whatever id is asked.

Change a screen schedule the caller set up for themselves (find#ScreenSchedules): its timing (cronExpression, a time pattern), format (renderMode: csv, xlsx, xsl-fo or html-print), skipping when empty (noResultsAbort Y or N), active interval (fromDate, thruDate), subject (emailSubject: plain text of at most 255 characters; one that holds an expression is refused, since the subject is expanded when the schedule runs) and pause (paused). Never its screen, saved find, user, group, template or location. A value not sent is kept, and clearFields names which of emailSubject, fromDate and thruDate to empty. Another user's schedule, a report schedule (store#Schedule's) and one that does not exist are refused alike (SCHEDULE_UNAVAILABLE); a value that is not one of these is VALUE_INVALID.
The report schedules userId owns, by name only (the owned-resource lookup of org.moqui.admin.IdentityServices): the viewer's own, or another user's for a holder of REPORT_OWNER_CHANGE.

Pause every report schedule userId owns (the owned-resource pause), marked owner-disabled, until transfer#DefinitionOwner hands each to a new owner: the viewer's own, or another user's for a holder of REPORT_OWNER_CHANGE. It reads no report.

Hand one report schedule (screenScheduledId), with its definition and the definitions that references which fromUserId owns, to toUserId (the owned-resource transfer): for fromUserId themselves or a holder of REPORT_OWNER_CHANGE. Refused unless toUserId is an active internal user who may store a schedule and reads the definition and every source it names. The schedule stays paused (transfer-pending) until the new owner resumes it, which repeats the audience check against the new owner's scope; nothing already delivered runs again, and the caller gains no report data.

The last outcome of each recipient of business alert rules, as states and safe reason codes, never a value or a series label: of the rules the viewer owns (one rule's with definitionId), each recipient by name; with received true, the deliveries to the viewer; with administrative true, every owner's business rules for a holder of ADMIN_TRANSFER_VIEW, as counters by rule (sent, skipped, failed, paused, last evaluated) without a title, a series or a recipient.

An alert rule the viewer reads with the state of each of its series (labels, state, since, last evaluated, the last value). A business rule's state is its owner's reading: instances are answered to its owner, and to a recipient of its audience whose scope fingerprint equals the owner's now; anyone else gets available false with a reason code (not-recipient, scope-differs, not-shared, ...) and no instance. A shipped rule is a template and has no state. ownerName is the owner's name, for anyone who reads the rule (none for a shipped rule, or when the owner's account is gone).
The alert rules userId owns, by name only (the owned-resource lookup): the viewer's own, or another user's for a holder of REPORT_OWNER_CHANGE.

Pause every alert rule userId owns (the owned-resource pause), marked owner-disabled, until transfer#AlertRuleOwner hands each to a new owner: the viewer's own, or another user's for a holder of REPORT_OWNER_CHANGE. It reads no state and no value.

Hand one alert rule (definitionId), with the shared silences and mute timings it names that fromUserId owns, to toUserId (the owned-resource transfer): for fromUserId themselves or a holder of REPORT_OWNER_CHANGE. Refused unless toUserId is an active internal user who may save definitions, reads the rule's sources and, for a group audience, may deliver to a group (NEW_OWNER_REFUSED). The rule stays paused (transfer-pending) until the new owner resumes it, which repeats the audience check against the new owner's scope; the caller gains no state and no value.
For the gitECA of a push or fetch: pull every enabled sync of the repository when its default branch changed.
